subject: Site readiness: Kube host fleet & data-paths — decisions required
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@stellacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Site readiness: Kube host fleet & data-paths — decisions required

Hi Jamie / Alex,

Thanks again for the kick-off yesterday. We’re starting the on-site prep for the StellaCare cluster and I put together a concise decision checklist so we can lock the deploy window next week. Can you confirm the items below by EOD Tuesday? If anything needs a call, flag it and we’ll book 30 minutes.

Summary (we need confirmations):
- Physical NIC topology: will each host present 2x10Gb + 1x1Gb mgmt to the leaf or 2x25Gb? Please list model if possible.
- L2 segmentation: VLAN ranges for tenant traffic, storage (iSCSI/roce), and mgmt. Any existing filtering we should mirror?
- Storage backend: prefer local NVMe pool (direct-attached) or central SAN (iSCSI/FC). Provide preferred FSType (ext4/xfs) and whether multipath is required.
- Encryption & KMS: Are you providing an on-prem KMS (HSM) endpoint or do you want Redwood to manage an encrypted keystore? We need hostname, certs, and ACLs.
- NTP & time sync: source for cluster NTP (internal vs public).
- BGP / eBGP peering: will you hand off at leaf with BGP sessions or a routed transit? If BGP, please share ASN and acceptable prefixes.
- Retention & RTO: desired PV snapshot cadence and RTO for model checkpoints (hours).

Attachments: fleet_topology_v1.pdf (draft), data-paths-latency-matrix.csv (baseline IO), kms_integration_notes.md (questions).

Operational asks:
- Please provide a point of contact for rack-level power limits and PDUs (name & onsite phone).
- Confirm whether maintenance windows are nightly 02:00–04:00 local time or a weekend block.

Next steps after confirmations: a short runbook for host imaging, a small 3-node bake cluster for validation, then full fleet imaging.

Best,
Michael Grant
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@stellacare.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Site readiness: Kube host fleet & data-paths — decisions required

Michael — thanks, this is great and very actionable. Quick answers below; I copied Alex on storage specifics.

- NICs: majority of racks are 2x25Gb (Mellanox CX5) + 1x1Gb mgmt. We’ll provide switch models in a follow-up spreadsheet.
- VLANs: tenant 1000–1099, storage 2000–2009, mgmt 3000. We run ACLs on the leafs for east/west segmentation.
- Storage: prefer local NVMe for performance (models are Samsung PM1733). We do have an iSCSI SAN for backups. Multipath not required for local; XFS preferred.
- KMS: we have an internal Vault cluster (on-prem) reachable at vault.stellacare.local. I’ll send certs via secure link.
- NTP: internal NTP pool is preferred (ntp1.stellacare.local, ntp2).
- BGP: We terminate at the leaf; ASN 64520. We can peer with a pair of top-of-rack routers — will share prefixes.
- Retention: model checkpoints: daily snapshot, retain 14 days; RTO target = 2 hours for critical inference models.

POC for power: Mark Liu, +1 (408) 555-0102 (rack power engineer). Maintenance window: preferred weekend window Sat 02:00–06:00 local.

We’ll upload the switch inventory and cert bundle by EOD Monday.

—Jamie
Jamie Park
Head of CloudOps, StellaCare Health
jamie.park@stellacare.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jamie Park <jamie.park@stellacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Site readiness: Kube host fleet & data-paths — decisions required

Thanks for the clarity, Jamie. A few technical confirmations and proposed defaults so the ops team can script imaging:

1) Host NICs: treat as 2x25Gb + 1x1Gb mgmt. We’ll configure bond0 for pod traffic (LACP active) and keep mgmt on a separate interface.
2) VLAN plan: use the ranges Jamie provided; we’ll annotate the leaf ACLs to ensure storage VLAN 2000–2009 is only reachable from kube hosts via iSCSI ports (3260) and RDMA if enabled.
3) Storage profile: default to local NVMe pool. Provisioned volumes will use XFS, with Kubernetes CSI driver configured for direct attach. For backups, we’ll snapshot to the on-prem iSCSI SAN nightly and push a copy offsite to S3-compatible object storage (encrypted).
4) KMS / Vault: we will integrate Redwood's node agent with your Vault endpoint. Action items for your team: provide Vault IP(s), token-scoped service account, and cert bundle. We’ll supply a small test container that exercises encrypt/decrypt prior to the bake run.
5) Time sync: will use ntp1.stellacare.local as primary; fallback to pool.ntp.org.
6) BGP: we’ll peer to your leafs using ASN 64520. Please confirm the two peer IPs so we can generate neighbor configs.
7) Snapshot & retention: implement daily snapshots for checkpoints with an operator that keeps 14 retention and enables on-demand export for long-term archiving. RTO = 2 hours target; we’ll run a recovery drill during the bake phase.

Imaging plan & bake cluster:
- Week 0: generate PXE image + ignition with Vault creds withheld (to be injected via secure channel).
- Week 1: spin a 3-node isolated bake cluster in rack 3, validate NVMe performance with the attached latency matrix.
- Week 2: full fleet imaging and staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Open items for your infra team (quick list):
- Vault endpoint & certs (secure link)
- Two BGP neighbor IPs + allowed prefixes
- Switch model list and serials for our inventory CSV

I’ll prepare the runbook and post to the Drive link (JIRA-OPS-1126). If we hit any blockers on cert transfer, Laura can assist with secure transport.

Cc’ing Laura to confirm we have the right SRE on-call for the bake.

—Dev Patel
